newsitem.title: VATICAN: Albanian bishops urge Europe do more.
newsitem.headline: Albanian bishops urge Europe do more.

text.p: Albania's Roman Catholic bishops called on European countries on Thursday to do more to help the Balkan country emerge from poverty and chaos.
In an appeal issued through the Vatican after meeting last week in the town of Lezhe, the six bishops said it was primarily up to Albanians themselves to resolve the country's problems.
They voiced appreciation for the provision of foreign relief aid, now flowing in under the protection of an Italian-led multinational security force, but said emergency supplies were not enough.
"We, the Bishops of Albania, address an appeal to Europe to consider the question of Albania with greater and more effective commitment than it has done until now," the statement said.
"With its large investments, Europe should contribute more to the economic development of Albania.
"...In our case it is not just a matter of humanitarian aid, but above all of spiritual values which can only be instilled through education in true democracy," the bishops said.

Albania, Europe's poorest country, has been rocked by violence and anarchy since the collapse in January of fraudulent get-rich-quick investment schemes into which many of the country's people had sunk their life savings.
Nearly 300 people have died in the violence, with rebels in control of much of the south after an armed insurrection erupted in late February and state armouries were emptied of their weapons.
The tiny state was Europe's most isolated country for more than four decades under the iron-fisted rule of late Stalinist leader Enver Hoxha.
Religion was officially banned for nearly 30 years. The country has a mixed population of Roman Catholics, Orthodox Christians and Moslems.
